name: Capacity Operation Events Monitoring Pipeline
description: Stream near-real-time Fabric capacity operation-level telemetry (per-operation CU consumption, duration, throttling, workspace/item attribution) into Real-Time Intelligence for root-cause analysis and automated alerting. Wires the FabricCapacityOperationEvents eventstream source to an Eventhouse (KQL) destination for retention/analysis, then optionally a Reflex/Activator trigger for no-code throttling alerts. Answers 'which operations are causing capacity pressure?' beyond the high-level Overview events.
prerequisites: Capacity administrator (capacity operation events are admin-scoped)
The capacity UUID to monitor (fabio capacity list)

steps.command: fabio capacity list --query "[].{name: displayName, id: id}"
steps.description: Find the capacity UUID you want to monitor.
steps.notes: Capacity Operation Events answer 'which operations are causing it?'; Capacity Overview Events answer 'what is happening to my capacity?' — use both for full visibility.

steps.description: Create the Eventhouse (with its default KQL database) that will retain the operation telemetry for historical analysis and dashboards.
steps.notes: Streaming into Eventhouse gives retention + KQL analytics over the raw operational signals.

steps.description: Create the eventstream that will carry the capacity operation events.
steps.notes: One eventstream can fan out to multiple destinations (Eventhouse for analysis, Activator for alerts).

steps.description: Add the capacity operation events source. eventScope is one of Tenant, Capacity, Workspace, Item, SubItem (PascalCase).
steps.notes: Optional: narrow with "includedEventTypes" and "filters" (e.g. [{"operatorType":"StringIn","key":"data.operationType","values":["..."]}]). Scope to a single capacity with capacityId, or Tenant for all.

steps.command: fabio eventstream add-destination --workspace $WS --id $ES_ID --name to_eventhouse --destination-type Eventhouse --input-node cap_ops --properties '{...eventhouse/kql-db reference...}'
steps.description: Route the source into the Eventhouse/KQL database for retention and KQL analysis.
steps.notes: Use fabio eventstream list-components --category destination to see destination shapes. --input-node wires this destination to the cap_ops source node.

steps.description: Verify the source -> destination wiring before relying on it.
steps.notes: Confirms the graph: FabricCapacityOperationEvents source feeding the Eventhouse destination.

steps.command: fabio kql-database query --workspace $WS --id $KQL_DB_ID --query "<Table> | where data.throttling... | summarize by data.workspaceId"
steps.description: Analyze operation telemetry in KQL: which refreshes consumed the most CU, which operations were throttled, which workspaces drive pressure.
steps.notes: See the RTI/KQL skill for schema discovery (kql-database list-tables / describe-table).

steps.command: fabio reflex create --workspace $WS --name throttle_alert    # then define a rule on the capacity-events stream
steps.description: Optional no-code alerting: create a Reflex (Activator) trigger to fire when high-cost operations exceed a threshold or throttling is detected, driving notification/remediation workflows.
steps.notes: This mirrors the blog's 'Microsoft Activator for designing automated triggers with no code'.

tips: Capacity Operation Events are a PREVIEW Real-Time Hub source; pair them with Capacity Overview Events for both detailed and high-level views.
Each event carries workspace + item details, CU consumption, operation duration, start time, and smoothing-window attribution — ideal for per-operation root-cause analysis.
Stream into Eventhouse for historical retention; add an Activator/Reflex trigger for near-real-time alerts on throttling or high-cost operations.
Scope with eventScope + capacityId to avoid ingesting tenant-wide volume when you only care about one capacity.
Microsoft's Capacity Events Accelerator (fabric-toolbox) is a prebuilt starting point for the same pattern.
